hypothesis: A decode token's attention layer is several device round trips with host arithmetic between them, and under WDDM the trips cost more than the kernels; running the layer as one round trip (one CUDA graph per layer, the CPU reference's order of operations) cuts the attention time per token without changing any result.
model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 architecture, abliterated weights (same shapes), safetensors, native FP8/FP4
command: make -C c cuda-dsv4-dg-dll cuda-dsv4-dll && make -C c -f Makefile.deepseek-v4 ARCH=native CUDA=1 deepseek-v4; deepseek_v4 <model> --prompt-file prompt3k.txt --max-tokens 36 --memory-gb 16 with the environment in config; tok_s = 35 / after_first from the engine's `timing` line (decode throughput after the first token)
